questions.text: How many people regularly use AI tools in your day-to-day work?

options.label: Just me
2–3 people
4–10 people
11–50 people

questions.text: What’s your primary AI setup today?

options.label: Personal AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) with no structured knowledge base
AI + personal knowledge base (Obsidian, Notion, Apple Notes, etc.)
DIY AI-memory system (Open Brain, NotebookLM, Obsidian, Claude Projects, etc.)
Multiple AI tools stitched together across workflows
Not using AI for business operations yet

questions.text: When someone else needs context from your AI work — a team member, contractor, or partner — how does that happen today?

options.label: They ask me directly — I’m the only one who uses AI
I copy-paste or screenshot the relevant parts
We share an account or workspace (everyone sees everything)
We have separate setups but manually sync a shared knowledge base
N/A — I work solo and don’t share AI context with anyone

questions.text: If you brought someone new into your work tomorrow — a hire, a contractor, a co-founder — how long before they could make AI-informed decisions using your existing business context?

options.label: Days to weeks — they’d need to rebuild context from scratch
A few hours — I’d walk them through my setup manually
Under an hour — they’d access shared context with their own role
N/A — I work solo with no plans to bring anyone in

questions.text: Think about a significant business decision you made 3–6 months ago — a pricing change, a vendor switch, a strategic pivot. Without asking anyone else, what can your system tell you?

options.label: I can’t find it — the decision lives in my head or scattered across tools
I can find what was decided, but not why or what alternatives were considered
I can find what was decided and why — but not whether it worked
The full picture: what, why, alternatives considered, outcome, and lessons learned
N/A — I haven’t been operating long enough for this to apply

questions.text: If you stopped checking your dashboards, inboxes, and AI tools for two full weeks, what would happen to your business?

options.label: Things would fall through — nothing catches and escalates on its own
I have some automated alerts, but they’re noisy — real issues would get buried
Critical items would be caught, but smaller things would slip
My system reliably catches and escalates what matters, with high signal-to-noise
I don’t use dashboards — I track everything manually or in my head

questions.text: After your busiest week of the month, how much of what actually happened is captured in your system — without anyone stopping to document it?

options.label: Almost nothing — if nobody logs it, the system doesn’t know
Some things automatically (email threads, calendar, transcripts) — but not decisions or context
Most operational activity is captured, but there are gaps in the important stuff
Nearly everything — decisions, context, follow-ups captured during normal work
I don’t think about capture — I just work and hope to remember what matters

questions.text: When your AI recommends a course of action — a strategy, a hire, a vendor choice — what challenges that recommendation before you act on it?

options.label: Nothing — I review the output myself and decide
I ask the same AI to ‘find weaknesses’ in its own recommendation
I manually get a second opinion from a different AI tool or a person
A separate agent or process automatically reviews AI output before I see it
I don’t use AI for recommendations — just information retrieval

questions.text: How do you track what your business spends on AI tools and whether that spending is worth it?

options.label: I don’t track it — it’s negligible or bundled into subscriptions
I see the total bill but can’t connect it to specific workflows or outcomes
I have rough estimates per team or project, but no precise attribution
I can produce per-workflow cost-to-outcome attribution for most of my AI spend
I only use free tiers — cost isn’t a factor yet

questions.text: How important is it that you could switch AI providers or tools without losing your setup?

options.label: Critical — I won’t commit to any single platform
Important — I prefer portability but would accept some lock-in for enough value
Nice-to-have — if the system works, I’ll stay
Not important — I’d rather have a great integrated system

questions.text: How quickly do you need to be operational with your AI system?

options.label: Today — I can’t wait weeks for configuration
Within a week — I need fast time-to-value
A few weeks is fine if the system is significantly better
I’ll invest months in setup for something that truly transforms my operations

questions.text: What’s your comfort level with AI spending for business operations?

options.label: Free or near-free only — I’m not ready to invest in AI tooling
Under $50/month — I’ll pay for clear value but keep it lean
$50–500/month — I’m investing in AI as a real operational tool
$500+/month — AI is a core business expense and I budget for it

questions.text: How often do you hit limits with your current AI setup that make you think ‘there must be a better way’?

options.label: Rarely or never — my setup works well for what I need
Occasionally — maybe once a month
Regularly — it’s a weekly frustration
Constantly — it’s a daily pain point
I don’t use AI for operations yet — so I haven’t hit limits

questions.text: In the next 12 months, what’s most likely to change about how your business uses AI?

options.label: Not much — I’m happy with my current approach
I’ll add a few more AI tools to my personal stack
I’ll need to bring team members into my AI workflows
I’ll need AI handling more complex, multi-step business processes
I’m not sure yet — still exploring where AI fits

fridayos_fit.description: You're hitting structural walls that an integrated AI operating system addresses.
fridayos_fit.cta_primary: Join the Friday OS beta waitlist

diy_identity.label: Open Brain
diy_identity.description: An open-source shared-memory layer so Claude, ChatGPT, and other tools all work from one picture of you and your business.

diy_attention.label: NotebookLM
diy_attention.description: Google's free, hosted tool for chatting with your own documents — answers grounded only in the sources you give it. Nothing to install.

diy_decision_memory.label: Obsidian + Claude
diy_decision_memory.description: A local, backlinked knowledge graph for decisions and their reasoning, connected to Claude so your AI can read and write your decision log.

diy_write_back.label: basic-memory
diy_write_back.description: Lets your AI write what it learns back into plain Markdown files you own, so insights persist across tools and sessions.

diy_governance.label: Watch this wall
diy_governance.description: There's no DIY tool we'd stake our name on for governance yet — controlling and auditing what your AI can access is a platform-class problem.

diy_economics.label: OpenRouter
diy_economics.description: Routes your AI calls through one hosted dashboard so you can see spend per model and workflow and set usage alerts. No infrastructure to run.

stay_put.label: Stay where you are
stay_put.description: Your current setup is working. The framework's job is to tell you when it's not — and right now, it's not.

approaching_walls.label: Watch these walls
approaching_walls.description: You're approaching structural limits. Here's what to watch for.
